title: docs(types): correct BaseSchema.hidden's JSDoc to the single hide path
body:
Fixes #7088

`BaseSchema.hidden`'s JSDoc promised a behaviour the renderer has never had. This corrects the comment, and adds the pin that keeps it true. **Comment-only — no behaviour moves.** Clause ② `no`, per the ruling.

## What the renderer measurably does — measured, not paraphrased

Read at `86be0a90f` against `origin/main` `fda1247b3`:

| key | what `SchemaRenderer` does | outcome |
|---|---|---|
| `visible: false` | `shouldHide` leg 2 returns `!evaluateVisibilityPredicate(newSchema.visible, 'visible')` | `_hidden = true` |
| `hidden: true` | `shouldHide` leg 5 returns `evaluateVisibilityPredicate(newSchema.hidden, 'hidden')`, un-negated | `_hidden = true` |

`_hidden` has **exactly one consumer** in the package — `if (evaluatedSchema._hidden) return null;` in `SchemaRenderer.tsx` — so both keys converge on the same early return and the component is not rendered. Three measurements behind that:

- `grep -rn "_hidden" packages/react/src` outside tests: the assignment in the `shouldHide` block, the `return null`, and the destructure that **strips** the key from the forwarded DOM props. No fourth site.
- a grep for a `visibility` style set to `hidden` across `packages/*/src`: **zero** hits. Nothing emits that style for either key, so "rendered but not visible" was never reachable.
- `grep -rn "display: none"` in `packages/react/src`: **zero** hits — the `visible` comment's `display: none` claim rests on the same false premise, so it is corrected in the same stroke.

By the time `_hidden` is read the key that set it is gone, so no branch could tell the two apart even if one wanted to.

## Where the two blocks actually were

Line numbers had drifted from the card (`:296-301` / `:262-264`); both located by symbol:

| block | card said | actual on `fda1247b3` |
|---|---|---|
| `hidden?: boolean;` | 296-301 | JSDoc **295-300**, declaration **301** |
| `visible?: boolean \| string;` | 262-264 | JSDoc **261-277**, declaration **278** |

The `visible` block had grown the objectui#4581 predicate-string paragraph since the card was filed; only its first two lines are touched, that paragraph is untouched.

## What the JSDoc now says

- `hidden: true` is **not rendered** — the renderer sets `_hidden` and returns `null`, exactly as for `visible: false`. No node kept, no `visibility: hidden`.
- The synonymity is recorded **as a decision**, with the declined alternative named, so the next reader does not read "two keys" as "two behaviours".
- Synonymous in **outcome** is not synonymous in **precedence**: every `visible*` leg is consulted first, so a declared `visible` — an empty one included — short-circuits `hidden`. That distinction is what makes the note safe to write; it is pinned already in `SchemaRenderer.expressions.test.tsx` and `SchemaRenderer.hiddenDeclaredGate.test.tsx`, and is cross-referenced rather than re-pinned.
- A corollary aimed at the next docs edit: `schema-reference.md`'s "Inverse of `visible`" row is the half describing shipped behaviour. **Unchanged, and it stays** — per the ruling, and because it was the near-miss that made this card worth filing.

## The pin, and its ablation

New: `packages/react/src/__tests__/SchemaRenderer.hiddenVisibleSynonymy.test.tsx` (2 cases).

The two halves were already pinned **separately** (`SchemaRenderer.expressions.test.tsx`: "does not render when visible is false", "hides when hidden is true"). What was not pinned is the claim the new JSDoc actually makes — that they hide **the same way**. Case 1 asserts the two rendered outputs against **each other**; case 2 asserts that `hidden: true` leaves no element at all, which is the retracted promise stated as unreachable. Precedence and the DOM-prop strip are deliberately not duplicated here.

**Red-then-green ablation**, run on the committed implementation:

- mutation: the `hidden` leg's `return evaluateVisibilityPredicate(newSchema.hidden, 'hidden');` becomes `return false;` — i.e. the declined "keep the node" differentiation.
- proven on disk **before** the run, not by an exit code: HEAD blob `7f9427de` vs post-mutation blob `5f49e22c`; anchored counts original `1 -> 0`, injected marker `0 -> 1`.
- **RED**: both cases fail, and the failure message is the differentiation's own signature — vitest reports the probe element (a `div` carrying `data-testid="probe-7088"`) where `null` was expected. The node survives, which is exactly what a `visibility: hidden` implementation would produce.
- restore proven **by state**: `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean, disk blob back to `7f9427de`, original count back to `1`, marker count `0`. `trap ... EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths resolved from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.
- **GREEN** on the restored tree. No rebuild was needed for either leg: the pin imports `../SchemaRenderer` by relative path, so vitest transforms the mutated source directly — which the red leg itself demonstrates.

## Verification — all at `86be0a90f`, tree clean

```
pnpm vitest run  SchemaRenderer.hiddenVisibleSynonymy  SchemaRenderer.expressions  SchemaRenderer.hiddenDeclaredGate
  -> Test Files 3 passed (3) · Tests 46 passed (46)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/types --filter @object-ui/react type-check
  -> packages/types: Done · packages/react: Done (after pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter "@object-ui/react^..." run build)
npx turbo run lint --filter=@object-ui/types --filter=@object-ui/react
  -> Tasks: 3 successful, 3 total · 0 errors (warnings are pre-existing; none on the edited lines)
pnpm check:control-bytes
  -> OK (scanned 6138 tracked text files)
pnpm changeset:check
  -> all three assertions pass
```

Not-measured trap checked rather than assumed: `tsc -p packages/react/tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists the new test file, so the react type-check green genuinely covers it.

Heavy runs went through the shared verify lock; the wall-clock figures it printed are shared-box seconds, not idle-box readings.

## Scope

Untouched, as fenced: any renderer behaviour; `content/docs/api/schema-reference.md`; `packages/types/src/blocks.*`, `index.ts`, `zod/index.zod.ts` (#7432); `zod/data-display.zod.ts` and `data-display.ts` (#7447). The zod mirror was checked and needs nothing — `base.zod.ts` describes `hidden` as "Hidden control", which makes no claim this change retracts. No compile-time ledger forced `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts`, so it is untouched too.

Filed out of scope while here: **#7455** — `hidden` is declared `boolean` while the renderer evaluates it as a predicate (expression-valued `hidden` is already pinned as working), making it the third key on `visible`/`disabled`'s evaluated path and the only one never widened. That is a declared-type change and needs its own ruling, exactly as #4580 did.

## Ruling

Comment [5494803259](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7088#issuecomment-5494803259) — 项目总监席, 总监批 #28, 2026-09-01, maintainer verbatim 「同意」:

> 1. **改 JSDoc**:`base.ts:296-301` 按单一隐藏路径改写 —— `hidden: true` 与 `visible: false` 同路返回 null(不渲染),⛔ 不再承诺 `visibility: hidden`;`:262-264` 的 `visible` 注释相应对齐;
> 2. **同义性记录在案**:两键行为同义是本裁决确认的决定,JSDoc 加一句注记防下一个读者把「两个键」读成「两种行为」;
> 3. **分化不做**:「保留节点 + `visibility: hidden`」是发布 prop 上的行为变更,零具名消费者(无 a11y/动画用例提出)—— 真用例出现 ⇒ 带消费者的特性卡回箱;
> 5. Clause-②:no(注释级,行为零位移)。

That supersedes comment [5489588894](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/issues/7088#issuecomment-5489588894), which had relabelled the card `needs-user-decision`; a reader going top-to-bottom meets the open fork first.
